target.title: feat(doctor): warn about in-flight cron jobs
target.body:
feat(doctor): warn about in-flight cron jobs

## What Problem This Solves

Persisted cron jobs carry a mutable `state.runningAtMs` marker. The scheduler sets it
while a run is active and clears it on completion. If the gateway is killed mid-run, the
marker is left behind. `openclaw cron list` and `openclaw cron show` derive the status
`running` from a truthy `state.runningAtMs` (`computeStatus` in
`src/cli/cron-cli/shared.ts`), so a stale marker makes a job look like it is running even
though nothing is executing it. `openclaw doctor` currently says nothing about this state,
and the gateway silently marks these runs interrupted the next time it starts
(`start` → `markInterruptedStartupRun` in `src/cron/service/ops.ts`). The operator is left
with a `cron list` that disagrees with reality and no diagnostic that explains it.

## Why This Change Was Made

`openclaw doctor` is the place operators look when cron state looks wrong, and it already
reads the cron store to report legacy-migration and model-override issues. Adding an
observer-only advisory there closes the gap without new config, new commands, or any state
mutation. The count uses the same predicate the gateway startup uses to decide which runs
to mark interrupted (`typeof state.runningAtMs === "number"`), so the count matches exactly
the set of runs a gateway restart would mark interrupted. The wording is deliberately conditional ("If no
gateway is currently executing them…") so it remains accurate even if doctor is run while a
gateway is genuinely mid-run — it reports a store fact plus the documented startup behavior,
and never claims doctor repaired anything.

## User Impact

Running `openclaw doctor` (no `--fix` needed) now surfaces, under the existing `Cron`
heading, how many cron jobs are still marked in-flight, notes that `cron list` shows them as
`running`, explains that leftover markers get marked interrupted on the next gateway start,
and points to `openclaw cron list` / `openclaw cron show <id>` for review. No behavior
changes for the scheduler, the store, or `--fix`; jobs without a `runningAtMs` marker see no
new output.

## Evidence

**Observer-only, no store write.** The advisory is emitted before the clean-store early
return in `maybeRepairLegacyCronStore`, so the repair prompt and every store-write path
(`applyLegacyCronStoreRepair`) are never reached. It never mutates `state.runningAtMs`,
never marks a run interrupted, and does not depend on `--fix`.

Deterministic tests (`src/commands/doctor/cron/index.test.ts`, +60) exercise the real
`maybeRepairLegacyCronStore` against a real SQLite cron store:

- one in-flight job → advisory emitted, repair prompt **not** called, persisted
  `runningAtMs` preserved, no `lastRunStatus` written;
- two in-flight jobs → advisory pluralizes;
- no marker → no advisory.

Focused suite `src/commands/doctor/cron/index.test.ts`: **50/50** (47 existing + 3 new).
`oxfmt --check` clean on both files; `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` pass; `git diff --check` clean.

Production-path capture — real `openclaw doctor` cron path (`maybeRepairLegacyCronStore`)
with a real SQLite store under an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, no mocks:

```
◇  Cron ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  1 cron job is still marked in-flight (`state.runningAtMs` is set), so   │
│  openclaw cron list shows it as `running`.                               │
│  - If no gateway is currently executing it, the marker is left over      │
│    from an interrupted run; the gateway marks such runs interrupted the  │
│    next time it starts.                                                  │
│  - Review with openclaw cron list or openclaw cron show <id>.            │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

Post-run store read confirmed observer-only: repair prompt called = false; persisted
`state.runningAtMs` unchanged; `state.lastRunStatus` = undefined; `updatedAtMs` unchanged
(no store write).
